source_text: III. Ἀλλὰ χάρις τῷ θεῷ· κατὰ πάντων γὰρ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν. Ὃ γὰρ γενναιότατος Γερμανικὸς ἐπερρώννυεν αὐτῶν τὴν δειλίαν διὰ τῆς ἐν αὐτῷ ὑπομονῆς· ὃς καὶ ἐπισήμως ἐθηριομάχησεν. Βουλομένου γὰρ τοῦ ἀνθυπάτου πείθειν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγοντος τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ κατοικτεῖραι, ἑαυτῷ ἐπεσπάσατο τὸ θηρίον προσβιασάμενος, τάχιον τοῦ ἀδίκου καὶ ἀνόμου βίου αὐτῶν ἀπαλλαγῆναι βουλόμενος. Ἐκ τούτου οὖν πᾶν τὸ πλῆθος, θαυμάσαν τὴν γενναιότητα τοῦ θεοφιλοῦς καὶ θεοσεβοῦς γένους τῶν Χριστιανῶν, ἐπεφώνησεν· Αἶρε τοὺς ἀθέους· ζητείσθω Πολύκαρπος.
pass_a_gloss: But grace to God; for it did not have strength against all. For the most well-born Germanicus was strengthening their cowardice through the endurance in him; who also beast-fought in a marked way. For when the proconsul was wanting to persuade him and saying to pity his age, he drew the beast upon himself having used force, wanting to be set free more quickly from their unjust and lawless life. From this then all the multitude, having wondered at the nobleness of the God-beloved and God-revering race of the Christians, cried out: Take away the godless; let Polycarp be sought.
pass_b_english: But thanks be to God, for it did not prevail against them all. For the most courageous Germanicus put strength into their fearfulness by the steadfast endurance that was in him, and he met the wild beasts in a way that made him renowned.

When the proconsul wanted to persuade him and kept telling him to have pity on his youth, he compelled the issue and drew the beast upon himself, since he wanted to be delivered all the sooner from their unjust and lawless manner of life. At this, therefore, the whole crowd, filled with wonder at the nobility of the God-beloved and God-fearing people of the Christians, shouted: Away with the atheists; let Polycarp be searched out.
